subject: Re: Modular licensing for Private/VPC deployment — unbundle request
messages:
From: Lara Proctor <lara.proctor@medleaf.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medleaf.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Modular licensing for Private/VPC deployment — can you unbundle?

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the overview last week. As we scope the pilot and long-term deployment for MedLeaf, procurement has asked whether Redwood can provide an itemized (unbundled) commercial structure for the Private/VPC offering.

Specifically, they want:
- A stand‑alone platform fee (annual) separated from per-node licensing
- Support tiers (standard / enhanced / enterprise) with explicit hours, SLAs, and on‑call uplift for each
- Optional implementation retainer and one‑time migration credit language
- An amortized pricing example over 36 months and an alternate 12‑month pilot price

I attached our RFP (MedLeaf_RFP_2026.pdf). Procurement also noted they may treat platform fees as OPEX vs capital and would like contract language to support either treatment.

Can you send a short unbundled proposal and a matrix showing how support add‑ons and on‑call would be priced? Time is a bit sensitive — procurement wants a draft by Thu 5/7 EOD PT.

Best,
Lara

--
Lara Proctor
VP, Procurement
MedLeaf Health
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Proctor <lara.proctor@medleaf.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Modular licensing for Private/VPC deployment — can you unbundle?

Hi Lara —

Appreciate the RFP and the clarity on procurement's framing. Short answer: yes, we can provide an unbundled commercial structure and amortization examples. I'll outline below the high-level components we'll include and attach an initial pricing matrix for your review. Full SOW/contract language will follow once we agree on the commercial structure.

High-level components we'll separate:
1) Platform fee (annual) — optional amortization across contract term; covers control plane, roadmap, portal, and basic telemetry retention.
2) Private deployment license (per-node or per-GPU pool) — options for seat/node mixes and metered consumption variants.
3) Support tiers — Standard (business hours), Enhanced (extended hours + 24/7 paging for Sev1), Enterprise (dedicated on-call rotation + faster RTOs). We'll call out on‑call uplift as a % of base support.
4) Implementation retainer (one‑time) — fixed days for onboarding, migration credit options tied to committed term.

Attached: Initial_Pricing_Options_v1.xlsx with a modular matrix and two term examples (12m pilot, 36m amortized).

Quick question to make the matrix accurate: can you confirm expected steady‑state token throughput (approx daily average), and whether MedLeaf prefers per-node licensing or a per‑seat for their app developers? If you can give a ballpark by EOD Wed 5/6, we can hit the Thu deadline.

I'll bring Vanessa into the thread — she'll propose the formal pricing bands and discounting guardrails.

Regards,
Sofia
Director, Enterprise Sales (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Proctor <lara.proctor@medleaf.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Modular licensing for Private/VPC deployment — draft pricing matrix

Hi Lara, Sofia —

Looping in Mark and Marissa for pricing and ops notes. Sofia: thanks for the ask + matrix. Lara: a couple of practical constraints from our side and a recommended path to speed procurement approval:

1) We can present platform fee as either an upfront invoice or an amortized quarterly schedule — both are commercially equivalent; we'll provide language to support OPEX treatment (statement that customer can capitalize if they prefer).

2) Support tiers (high level):
   - Standard: 9x5 email + portal, 24hr response for Sev1
   - Enhanced: 12x5 + 4hr response for Sev1, on‑call escalation out of hours (paid uplift)
   - Enterprise: 24x7 with dedicated rotation and 1hr response for Sev1, includes quarterly business reviews.

3) Discounts / credits: for multi‑year commitments we can apply a platform fee amortization and implementation credit (one‑time) based on commit band. For a 36m commit we typically offer a platform fee credit equal to 10–20% of the first year fee, tiered by commit size. For a 12m pilot we can offer a pilot discount of 15% on platform fee only (no support uplift).

4) Migration credit and escrow: we can include a one‑time migration credit up to X days of engineering time — let's define X after we see the migration scope.

I've attached a simplified pricing table (extracted to keep the email small). If you want a full line‑item workbook, we can send that to procurement directly and include the SOW redline template.

Action items: Lara — confirm expected steady state throughput and preferred licensing unit (per‑node vs per‑seat) by EOD Wed. If procurement prefers, I'm happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through the matrix.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Head of Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
From: Lara Proctor <lara.proctor@medleaf.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medleaf.com, Ben Carter <ben.c@impl-consult.io>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 08:51:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Modular licensing for Private/VPC deployment — draft pricing matrix

Hi Vanessa / Sofia —

Thanks — that looks promising. A few clarifications from procurement:
- MedLeaf is leaning to treat the platform fee as OPEX for budgeting, but they want contract text that doesn't prevent capitalization later.
- For licensing unit: the internal architecture team prefers per‑node (GPU pool) but procurement wants an option that converts to per‑seat for developer tooling during year 2. Can you include a conversion factor in the pricing sheet?
- Migration: our estimate is ~12 engineer days of effort for the data ingress/mapping phase. Please propose the migration credit language that would cover that scope if we commit to 36 months.

One additional ask: for the 12‑month pilot we'd like an explicit exit cap on data egress costs and a 30‑day SLA for access to audit logs post‑termination. If those are spelled out we'll move quickly.

Would appreciate the revised workbook by EOD today (Thu 5/7) so procurement can circulate to legal.

Best,
Lara
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Modular licensing for Private/VPC deployment — final draft and next steps

Lara —

Thanks for the clarifications. Attached is the revised workbook and a one‑pager covering: platform fee amortization language, per‑node vs per‑seat conversion factors (we used a 1 node = 8 dev seats baseline for the conversion table), a migration credit clause that covers up to 12 engineer days for a 36m commit, and exit commitments for the 12m pilot (30‑day audit‑log access + a capped egress schedule).

Key points:
- 12m pilot: 15% platform discount, no migration credit, explicit 30‑day audit log access clause, egress capped at $X/month for first 3 months.
- 36m commit: platform fee amortized quarterly, migration credit of up to 12 engineer days (applied as a labor credit on the first invoice), and a tiered platform credit of 12% on Y band or 18% on Z band.

Next steps: 
- Sofia/Vanessa to share final workbook to procurement (I'll upload to the HubSpot deal: HS-9427).
- If legal requests redlines, we'll provide a marked SOW and contract template within 48 hours.
- Proposed pilot SOW draft and DocuSign envelope (placeholder) included here: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/DocuSign-Envelope-12345

If that aligns, can we schedule a 30m procurement call Mon 5/11 to sign off the pilot commercial? I'll include Markus from pricing and Marissa from CS to answer ops questions.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — I'll send the workbook to procurement now.

Regards,
Sofia
Director, Enterprise Sales (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
